ctx.x: But the thing that puzzled me mostly, was the man in the

pit. There was a fellow named James Vaughan, I think his name was. Well, he was conductor of this orchestra. Now, so I can tell you, that's what I wanted to do. And I worked a long -- it took me forty years to get to that place, where I conducted something. But I eventually got there.

Now, it was really a treat for me, at my age, to have seen Bert Williams do his slide, his funny slides, and tell his jokes. And George Walker, who was the greatest of the strutters. He could strut better than anybody. In fact, the strut, I think the black people took from the horses. Not the race horses, the show horses. And I think the way they'd raise their legs and throw it, just like you see a race horse, a show horse, not a race horse. But, Ada Walker was a very clever singer.
